items.claim: The one-verse unit's onset and both its mark disclosures are byte-true, but a divine-visitation catchword runs across both of its seams undisclosed, and the onset formula it leans on is a large class carried without a digit.
items.evidence: Every Hebrew run in the row matches its cited verse at byte tier, and both mark citations are correctly typed and correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness (setumah after MT 26:21 and after MT 27:1, single-witness, tier-3). What is missing is a cross-seam device. The row's own quoted onset verb is the middle link of a three-verse visitation chain on one root: לִפְקֹ֛ד עֲוֺ֥ן (oshb:Isa.26.21, byte tier) in the verse immediately before the row, יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) inside it, and פֶּ֚ן יִפְקֹ֣ד עָלֶ֔יהָ (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier) two verses after it; the consonantal skeleton stands in 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), so three sites in four consecutive verses is a dense local hook sitting on an oracle join and straddling BOTH of this row's edges. A byte-true device crossing a row's own seam argues continuity against that row unless it is disclosed, and neither edge here discloses it; the front-seam and close disclosures rest on the tier-3 single-witness marks alone. Second, the day-formula the row makes its onset driver is not a staged frame class and is a 45-verse object book-wide (sweep: 45 verses); the row carries no digit for it and does not distinguish the bare form it quotes from the waw-prefixed long form used two rows later in the same chapter.

items.claim: The song-frame identification at the onset verse and the close at 27:5 both rest on English rendering choices that the Hebrew of the cited verses does not carry.
items.evidence: The onset verse holds no song lexeme at all: the song noun and its cognate verb — יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר at the sung-song opening of oshb:Isa.26.1 (byte tier) — are absent from oshb:Isa.27.2, and that skeleton stands in 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses), the nearest being MT 26:1 itself. The song reading depends entirely on construing עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) as an order to sing — a rendering of a root that elsewhere in the book carries answer/afflict senses — so the signal class asserted for this row's onset has no lexical anchor in its own bytes; a frame claim needs the frame form present in the cited verse with the claimed role, and here no such form exists. The quote/gloss pairing then inverts the Hebrew: the row pairs the English “In that day, sing to her,” (web:Isa.27.2) with the full run בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) while placing “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2) outside that run — but כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), the words so rendered, are the third and fourth tokens INSIDE the run cited, standing before the verb; the 'formula, then introduced quotation' sequencing exists only because the English reorders the clause. The close is then argued from where the English quotation mark falls at web:Isa.27.5: the Hebrew carries no quotation delimitation anywhere in 27:2-5, and the material inside that English quotation is first-person divine speech, so the delimiter is a tier-4 rendering artifact, not a seam signal. The byte-grounded half of the close (a new opening at oshb:Isa.27.6) survives; the two English-only arms do not.

items.claim: The row's load-bearing reason for overriding a marked internal break is a plural English pronoun that does not stand in either of the two verses it is claimed for, and a feminine-suffix chain reaching back across the row's own front seam is undisclosed.
items.evidence: The rejected alternative turns on a plural pronoun said to open MT 27:7. oshb:Isa.27.7 opens with an interrogative-comparative construction, not a pronoun, and every suffix in it is third masculine singular: מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.27.7, byte tier). At the next verse the suffixes are third feminine singular: בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.8, byte tier). No plural pronoun stands in either verse, so the stated ground for setting aside the single-witness setumah recorded after MT 27:6 is available only in the English; the referential conclusion may still be reachable from the 3ms collective suffixes, but the row quotes no Hebrew at all from 27:7-8 and so never makes that argument. The undisclosed cross-seam evidence cuts the other way at the row's front edge: those 3fs suffixes continue the feminine-suffixed vineyard object of the preceding verses — נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier), matching the 3fs suffix on לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) — a byte-true grammatical chain straddling the 27:5|27:6 seam exactly where the row claims a fresh frame. Third, the onset הַבָּאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) is called a fresh formula; it is a bare participial form, not a member of any staged frame class in this book, and the English “In days to come” (web:Isa.27.6) supplies the noun that makes it read as a dated formula. The two Hebrew runs the row does quote reach byte tier, and both mark citations are correctly typed and keyed to the Hebrew witness.

items.claim: The split of the two adjacent day-formula verses is defended by a generalized pattern claim with no digit and by importing a different device class, while the linking form shared by both onsets is never weighed.
items.evidence: Both verses open with the identical waw-prefixed long form וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier; the same three tokens open oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier). That long form stands in 13 verses book-wide (sweep: 13 verses) and these two are its only adjacent pair, whereas the bare form treated as a unit onset at MT 27:1 and MT 27:2 is a 45-verse object (sweep: 45 verses) — two distinct spellings of the onset are being carried under one undifferentiated signal without disclosure, and no digit accompanies either. The row's stated ground, that each independent onset marks a separate proclamation 'as with the massa headers elsewhere in this frame', imports a different object: the header class is exactly 10 verse-initial sites, it bounds parent oracles, and it is not the day-formula at all — naming the swept object before arguing from it is the discipline the sentence skips. Nor is the counter-reading weighed: the waw prefix on both onsets is a sequencing form, so on the bytes the pair reads at least as readily as one continuing announcement as it does as two, and the row's own observation that both verses share the ingathering destination points the same way. The quoted run reaches byte tier, the setumah after MT 27:12 is correctly typed and disclosed single-witness, and the marks on both edges are correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness.
tier_citations: byte tier (pointed OSHB splice, re-verified against source bytes)

items.claim: The row closes the book's 27:13|28:1 frame seam without quoting the frame form that makes it a seam, and explains the missing mark there with a generalization the mark inventory contradicts.
items.evidence: The close is argued from the parent grouping rather than from the following verse's bytes. The byte arm of that seam is the verse-initial ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) opening the second woe series — a verse-initial site in the 20-member verse-initial woe inventory — which the row lists as a bare reference and never quotes, so its seam claim carries no byte evidence for the role it assigns to the following verse; a frame-based seam claim owes the frame form and its role in the cited verse's own bytes. The row then states that no mark follows MT 27:13 and that this is 'expected since it is the book's own frame-seam verse'. The inventory does not behave that way: of the eight verses that close a parent grouping in this architecture, five carry a mark (MT 12:6, MT 35:10 and MT 39:8 petuchah; MT 48:22 and MT 55:13 setumah) and only MT 1:1, MT 27:13 and MT 66:24 do not — so a tier-3 absence is being given explanatory work it cannot carry, on a layer where absence is never evidence in either direction. The row's own onset run and its trumpet run both match oshb:Isa.27.13 at byte tier, and the front-seam setumah after MT 27:12 is correctly typed and correctly keyed.
tier_citations: byte tier (pointed OSHB splice, re-verified against source bytes)

items.claim: The row declines an internal cut at 28:5 without disclosing that the verse opens with the very day-formula treated as a unit onset four times in the immediately preceding chapter and that the mark layer brackets exactly the rejected pair, while the counter-argument that holds it in is made from the English with no quoted form and no tier.
items.evidence: Inside the span, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) opens the verse — the identical verse-initial bare form treated as a unit-opening driver at MT 27:1 and MT 27:2, and in its waw-prefixed long form at MT 27:12 and MT 27:13; the formula is a 45-verse object book-wide (sweep: 45 verses) — and the parashah inventory records a setumah after MT 28:4 and another after MT 28:6 (single-witness, tier-3), bracketing precisely the 28:5-28:6 pair the row declines to cut. The rival sentence names neither corroboration, so both lines of support for the reading being rejected go undisclosed. The claim that holds the pair inside the span — that the crown motif keeps running — is asserted from the English “a crown of glory” (web:Isa.28.5) with no quoted form and no tier label, although the byte evidence exists and is strong: לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) is the third of exactly 3 sites of that noun in this chapter and 4 book-wide (sweep: 4 verses). The remnant identification is likewise English-only: לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) is the plain remnant noun, an object the book splits four ways on one root, correctly named as a class in the row but never quoted. The plene/defective observation is byte-true and also unquoted: שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) against שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י (oshb:Isa.28.3, byte tier). By contrast the crown pair the row does quote is handled correctly — the two runs differ at byte tier and agree once accents are stripped, exactly as labelled. Finally, all four mark references in this row are written under a WEB coordinate prefix although the parashah layer is read from the Hebrew witness and keyed to its numbering; the arithmetic lands only because this chapter is identity-numbered, and the same object is keyed to the Hebrew witness at MT 26:21, MT 27:1, MT 27:6, MT 27:11 and MT 27:12 in the material immediately preceding.
tier_citations: byte tier (pointed OSHB splice, re-verified against source bytes)

items.claim: Both of this row's edge arguments are made without any Hebrew, and the label it puts on its close-seam verse is contradicted by that verse's bytes.
items.evidence: The front seam is the row's strongest signal and carries no byte arm at all: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier) is one of exactly 3 verses in the book carrying that full summons formula (sweep: 3 verses — MT 1:10, MT 28:14, MT 66:5), and the addressee the row attributes to the English stands in the Hebrew as the last two of those tokens. The only Hebrew quoted in the row is the divine frame at oshb:Isa.28.16, which is internal to the span; that run is byte-true and the speaker class is correctly named as divine, which is the right discipline on a formula this book uses on both a divine and a royal-messenger side. The close is described as standing before a fresh vocative onset at 28:23, but oshb:Isa.28.23 contains no vocative element of any kind — its six tokens are four imperatives and two objects, with no addressee noun and no vocative particle — so the label sits on the wrong verse: the vocative in this neighbourhood is the addressee at the row's own opening. The bytes also carry an unclaimed bracket the row's bounds would have benefited from: the scoffer root recurs at אַל תִּתְלוֹצָ֔צוּ (oshb:Isa.28.22, byte tier), and that form and the noun at MT 28:14 each occur in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse each), so the root frames this span end to end. The doubled ketiv/qere at MT 28:15 is correctly disclosed and correctly kept out of quotation; the two mark references here, however, are keyed to the WEB witness while the ketiv/qere reference in the same list is keyed to the Hebrew one — the same object cannot take both keys.
tier_citations: byte tier (pointed OSHB splice, re-verified against source bytes)

items.claim: The summons the row builds its onset and its type on is quoted only in half, the vocative label it records is not present in that verse's bytes, and the disputation evidence actually inside the span goes uncited.
items.evidence: The row states that the Hebrew doubles the summons verb pair but quotes only the first colon; the doubling lives in the unquoted second colon הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier), so the run actually cited does not display the feature claimed for it. The signal recorded for the onset is a vocative, but oshb:Isa.28.23 has no addressee noun and no vocative particle — its six tokens are four imperative forms and two objects, imperative in both witnesses' renderings — so the label is byte-unsupported at the verse it is placed on; an imperative-summons onset is what the bytes there actually give. The type is then argued from that summons form alone, and the form is not distinctive: it stands in 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses — MT 1:10, MT 8:9, MT 28:23, MT 51:4, and MT 64:3 = web:Isa.64.4), spread across openings of very different speech classes, so it under-determines a disputation reading on its own. The evidence that would carry the typing is inside the row's own span and uncited: the verse-initial interrogatives הֲכֹ֣ל (oshb:Isa.28.24, byte tier) and הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.28.25, byte tier) open the case the row says the unit is making. The close against the following woe onset is byte-defensible and the setumah after MT 28:29 is correctly typed, though it too is keyed to the WEB witness rather than to the Hebrew one the layer is read from.
tier_citations: byte tier (pointed OSHB splice, re-verified against source bytes)
